method: Stems and options were printed from each year's key file with the recorded answer stripped, then every solved item was re-answered before any comparison.
independence: NOT independent: the same solver and the same corpus text produced both passes. Agreement is a consistency signal only and promotes nothing; it satisfies neither branch of ADR-0003's derived-verified test.
verdict: 48 raw disagreements across 321 re-answered items; all 48 adjudicated by re-derivation in favour of the recorded answer; zero key entries changed.

60.note: Algal bloom is driven by N, P and K, option A. The second pass answered on the classic carbon/nitrogen/phosphorus formulation, which the option set does not offer.

63.note: Aircraft noise uses the L10(18-hour) index, option C. The second pass picked Lepm, a different metric.

65.note: Stability is DALR > ELR, option C. The second pass had the inequality backwards.

7.note: Pair of lines: expanding (m1 y + n1)(l2 x + n2) gives 2fg = ch, option C. Verified on 2,000 random factorisations: zero violations of C and zero cases where B held. An earlier claim in prose that the key was wrong is retracted here.

8.note: The segment runs z = 5 to z = 3, so z = 0 lies beyond the far point: the division is external, 5:3, option B.

10.note: y = 5 + sin(x - 5) lies in [4, 6] and never reaches zero: option A, it does not cut the axis.

16.note: The normal at (a/2, sqrt3 a/2) is the radial line through the origin, y = sqrt3 x, i.e. sqrt3 x - y = 0, option D.

20.note: AB = (1,2,-1) and CD = (-3,-6,3) = -3 AB, so the lines are parallel, option D.

23.note: Ampere turns are H_iron l_iron + (B/mu0) l_gap = 219 + 1273.2 = 1492.2 AT, which is option A; the second pass answered 1942, which is option B's printed value.

25.note: Peak current is sqrt2 A, so stored energy is 0.5 x 0.1 x 2 = 0.1 J, option A.

59.note: Sound intensity is measured in W/m^2, option A; the decibel is a level, not an intensity unit.

69.note: Incineration runs at 900-1200 C, option A.

72.note: With the 300 N weight at d from the man end, moments about the boy end give d = 0.556 m, option C.

76.note: The diagonal of a square plate is a centroidal axis, so I = a^4/12, option B.

83.note: Rectangle about its base bh^3/3; triangle about its base bh^3/12; ratio 4:1, option C.

84.note: Closing speed is 10 km per 8 min = 75 km/h, so the third car's own speed is 75 - 40 = 35 km/h, option D.

87.note: E = 9GK/(3K + G), which is option D. The second pass picked option C, whose denominator 3K + 2G is a different elastic relation; substituting G = 3K/2 makes only D satisfy the standard identity E = 2G(1 + nu).

88.note: Volumetric strain of a thin closed cylinder is pD(5 - 4nu)/(4tE), which is option C; the second pass used the (2 - nu) open-cylinder form in option A.

93.note: For equal cross-sectional area the square section has the larger second moment about its bending axis (1.18x the circle), so the square beam is stronger, option C.

95.note: A mid-span load gives end slope W a^2/(2EI) with a = L/2, i.e. W L^2/(8EI), option C.

96.note: E2/E1 = L^2 A/(3I). For a 4 cm square section, A = a^2 and I = a^4/12, so the ratio is 12 L^2/(3 a^2) = 12/(3 x 0.0016) = 2500, which is option D. The second pass answered 1000, a value that follows only from a different section assumption.

97.note: Most conservative first: maximum principal stress, maximum shear, total strain energy, distortion energy, option A.

3.note: alpha = 2 beta, verified on three numeric triples with the ratio exactly 2.000000 each time.

11.note: x = (y-1) + e^-y with x(0) = 0 gives alpha = x(1) = e^-1, option C.

20.note: (1 + delta)(1 - nabla) is the identity operator, so it returns the sequence unchanged, option B.

34.note: Indian 230 V convention: phase red, neutral black, option C. Flagged in OPEN-DOUBTS B2 as convention-dependent.

44.note: Option C is the standard definition of context switching.

56.note: An audit covers monitoring, safety provisions and regulatory scrutiny; storing toxic chemicals is an operating activity, option B.

58.note: Stability requires the dry adiabatic lapse rate to exceed the ambient lapse rate, option B. The second pass chose option A (equality), which describes the neutral case, not a stable one.

71.note: With level unloaded arms the true weight is the geometric mean sqrt(W1 W2), option B.

80.note: Projectile speed is least at the apex, half the range, option B.

82.note: Polar second moment is A^2/(2pi) for the circle and A^2/6 for the square: ratio 3/pi, option A.

83.note: Each impact scales relative speed by e, so the same arc is retraced in t/e, option B.

88.note: sigma_h = 2 sigma with zero radial stress at the outer surface gives in-plane maximum shear sigma, option C.

99.note: sigma_x = sigma_y with no shear is isotropic, so every direction carries sigma_0, option B.

100.note: Same maximum shear stress gives strain energy 16 parts solid to 15 hollow, option D.

5.note: Sum of i.(j x k) over cyclic permutations is 3, so option B is the untrue statement.

9.note: Bisection halves the bracket, so the error is at most (b-a)/2^n, option D.

24.note: At 50 Hz the same voltage needs more flux, so the core saturates slightly and efficiency falls marginally, option D.

27.note: The rotor follows the field because induced current opposes relative motion: Lenz's law, option B.

30.note: Flux does not flow as current does, so option D is the false claim.

31.note: The three-point starter is for shunt motors, option B.

36.note: Closure of AC is only AC, so AC is not a candidate key, option A.

41.note: Infix to postfix needs one operator stack, option B. Flagged in OPEN-DOUBTS B1: option A's two-stack reading is also defensible.

50.note: printf with %d on a pointer prints the pointer value, i.e. an address, option D. Flagged in OPEN-DOUBTS B3: expected behaviour, not guaranteed.

59.note: Symmetric N2 and O2 develop no changing dipole moment in vibration, option C.
